newsitem.title: FRANCE: French songwriter and singer Mireille dies aged 90.
newsitem.headline: French songwriter and singer Mireille dies aged 90.

text.p: Mireille, a prodigious composer of popular French songs, died in a Paris clinic on Sunday after a lengthy illness, her family said. She was 90.

Mireille, whose real name was Mireille Hartuch, composed hundreds of songs during a long career, many of them with collaborator Jean Nohain. Among the best known were "Couches dans le Foin (Asleep in the Hay)", "Les Trois Gendarmes (The Three Gendarmes)" and "Le Petit Chemin (The Little Lane)".
"These are the tunes that we hum when we think of ripe fields of wheat, the joys of summer and young love," Prime Minister Alain Juppe said in a statement.
"We remember her smile, her charm and the indescribable presence of a great lady full of affection and tenderness".
After beginning her career as an actress and singer, she went on to become a singing teacher, training many of France's future pop stars including Francoise Hardy and Serge Lama.
Mireille founded the Little Conservatory of Song in Paris in 1955 and for the next 20 years was its director.
"She was a true, authentic artist," singer Charles Aznavour told France 3 television.
Mireille had lived alone in Paris since the death in 1976 of her husband, philosopher Emmanuel Berl.
